title: About
bodyHtml:
Expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) studies illuminate genomic variants that regulate specific genes and contribute to fine-mapping loci discovered via genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Efforts to maximize their accuracy are ongoing. Using 240 glomerular (GLOM) and 311 tubulointerstitial (TUBE) micro-dissected samples from human kidney biopsies from the NEPTUNE cohort, we discovered 5,371 GLOM and 9,787 TUBE eQTLs by incorporating kidney single-nucleus open chromatin data and transcription start sites as an "integrative prior" for Bayesian statistical fine-mapping. The use of an integrative prior resulted in higher resolution eQTLs illustrated by (1) smaller numbers of variants in credible sets with greater confidence, (2) increased enrichment of partitioned heritability for GWAS of two kidney traits, (3) an increased number of variants colocalized with the GWAS loci, and (4) enrichment of computationally predicted functional regulatory variants. A subset of variants and gene were validated experimentally in vitro and using a Drosophila nephrocyte model. More broadly, this study demonstrates that tissue-specific eQTL maps informed by single-nucleus open chromatin data have enhanced utility for diverse downstream analyses.

To make this data accessible to the community, we've developed an eQTL/CRE portal, www.nephqtl2.org. Here you can interactively search all our results, including eQTLs for GLOM and TUBE, snATAC-seq tracks, snRNA-seq counts and single-cell deltaSVM scores. Learn more about The Samson Lab at https://www.childrenshospital.org/research/labs/sampson-lab-research/lab-members.
